A quarter to five on Friday works great for me!

Hello! My name is Tom. I am twenty-five years old and I am from Canada. I live in Toronto with my sister. She is nineteen. Today I am at a language school. There are twelve students in my class. Two students are from Brazil, three are from Japan and one is from Italy. They are very friendly. My phone number is five five five, zero one two three.
Morning, Lucas! You're here early today. What time do you usually start work?
Hi, Chloe! Back in Brazil, I usually start at nine, so I get up at seven. Here in Toronto, I wake up at six thirty because of the time difference.
Do you drink coffee in the morning?
Yes, I do! I always have a big cup of black coffee before I check my emails. What about you?
I don't drink coffee at all. It makes me too anxious, so I always drink green tea.
And what about your husband, Dan? Does he work near here?
No, he doesn't. He works from home most days. He teaches graphic design online and finishes around five.
That's nice! Does he cook dinner during the week?
Yes, he does! He loves cooking, so he usually makes dinner, and I do the dishes. We never order delivery on weekdays.
I live in Boston. Do you live here?
No, I don't. I live in Chicago, but I work here.
I work in a bank. I don't like my job very much.

I work from home three days a week.
My brother works in finance and travels a lot.
She doesn't drink coffee, so she always orders tea.

Sara works in a bank. She starts at nine and finishes at five. She doesn't drive to work, she takes the bus. At lunch she eats a sandwich and drinks tea. She doesn't like coffee. In the evening she cooks dinner and watches a series. Her brother doesn't work on Saturdays, so he plays football with friends. Does Sara work on weekends? No, she doesn't.

— Anything else? — No, I'm good, thanks. That's all.

This is my desk. These are my books and those are my colleague's papers. That is my computer, and this is my phone. There is an umbrella under the desk. It is red. I have two pens and a notebook. These pens are new, but that notebook is old. Those windows are big, and the view is beautiful.

Awesome. What about lunch? Are there any good places to eat on this street?
Plenty! There's an amazing Italian restaurant right across from our building, and there's a pharmacy on the corner of Boylston Street and Clarendon.

On Sundays my family comes to my grandmother's house. She has a big garden. My father has two brothers, so I have two uncles and three cousins. My uncle's wife is called Rita. Her son has a dog. My mother's sister doesn't have children, but she has a cat. We have lunch together at one o'clock. After lunch, the children play in the garden and the adults talk.

Three or four bottles. By the way, do you have any news about Sarah's flight?
Yes, I have good news! She just sent me a message. She had a lot of luggage, so she took a taxi from the airport.
Awesome. Oh, can you give me some advice on the dessert? Should I make a chocolate cake or buy some ice cream?
Here's a piece of advice: buy ice cream! We don't have much time before seven!

She can't cook, so her husband cooks dinner. Can she drive? Yes, she can, but she doesn't have a car. This year she wants to learn French. She can already say hello and thank you!

My week is very busy. On Monday I have English class at half past seven. On Tuesday I have lunch with my sister at twelve. My dentist appointment is on Wednesday at a quarter to ten. On Thursday I work from home. On Friday evening I meet my friends at eight o'clock. My birthday is on the twelfth of March, so on Saturday we have a party. On Sunday I rest all day.

Mark gets up at six every day. He has breakfast at half past six, and then he goes to work. He usually starts work at eight and finishes at five. He has lunch at noon. After work, he goes home and cooks dinner. He never watches TV at night. He reads a book and goes to bed at ten. On the weekend, he gets up late and plays football with his friends.

I usually get up at six. I have breakfast and then I go to work.

Almost! I really enjoy creating training material, so I decided to add a few practical exercises.

Yes, please! Thank you for helping me, Kevin. I'm tired of looking at spreadsheets all day!
No problem. Send them to me, and I'll look at them before leaving the office.
Awesome. By the way, is Sarah coming to Boston next month to take the leadership course?
Yes, she is! I spoke to her ten minutes ago. She promised to book her flight tonight, and she asked us to reserve a hotel room for her.
Great! Let's not forget to send her the hotel link. Last time, David tried to book the hotel by himself and chose the wrong neighborhood!

I love music and I like cooking, but I hate waking up early. My brother likes football, but he doesn't like swimming. He loves pizza and he hates fish. My parents like travelling. They like Italy a lot, and they love the food there. My sister has a dog. She loves him and she walks him every morning. Do you like animals? I like them, but I don't like spiders!

My best friend is Dan. He is 28 years old. He is tall and strong. He has short dark hair and brown eyes. He has a small beard. Dan is very funny and friendly, but he is a bit shy with new people. He looks like his father. He loves cooking and playing football. I like him a lot.
Look, this is my friend Julia.
She is tall and thin. She has long brown hair and green eyes.

Great! Can I meet her on Saturday?
Yes, I'm looking for a black jacket.
I'm a medium. Can I try this one on?

It's nice. How much is it?

Today I need new clothes. First, I go to a shop and look at the shirts. This blue shirt is thirty dollars. That red one is forty-five. I try on the blue one, but it is too small. The assistant brings a bigger size. It fits! Then I look at shoes. These black shoes are eighty dollars, which is too expensive. I buy the shirt and a cheap pair of socks. Then I pay by card.
Hi, love! Can you talk right now, or are you in a meeting?
Hi! I can talk for a few minutes. I'm sitting in the hotel lobby right now, and I'm waiting for a taxi to the airport.
Wait — why are you going to the airport today? You usually fly back on Fridays!
I know, but this week we're visiting a client in Montreal. Sarah and David are coming with me — look, they're checking out at the front desk right now.
Oh, I see! Is it still snowing in Toronto?
No, it isn't snowing today, thank goodness. The sun is shining, but it's freezing outside! What are you guys doing at home?
Leo is doing his homework at the kitchen table, and I'm making dinner. Do you want to say hi to him?
I'd love to, but the taxi is arriving. Tell him hi for me! Talk to you tonight!
Can you talk right now, or are you working?

I usually work from home, but today I'm working at the office.
She's having lunch with a client at the moment.
I'm sorry, I don't understand what you mean.
Do you need any help with those boxes right now?

It is Saturday morning and everyone is busy. My mother is cooking in the kitchen. My father is reading the newspaper. My brother is playing a video game and my sister is talking on the phone. I am writing this text. The dog is sleeping next to the door. It is raining, so we are not playing outside. What are you doing right now?
Marina, it's almost five thirty! What are you doing this weekend? Do you have any plans?
Yes! Tomorrow morning I'm having breakfast with my friend Julia at eight thirty — we booked a table at that French bakery downtown.
Oh, nice! What are you going to do in the afternoon?
I'm going to buy a winter coat because next week is going to be freezing. Look at the dark clouds outside — it's going to rain in a few minutes!
Oh, no! I forgot my umbrella at home.
Don't worry, Kevin! I have an extra umbrella in my locker. I'll lend it to you!
Really? Thank you so much! I'll bring it back on Monday morning, I promise.
No problem! By the way, are you coming to the team dinner on Saturday night?
I'm not sure yet. My sister might visit us from New York, so I might stay home with her. I'll text you tomorrow to let you know!
What is the weather like on Saturday?
It is going to be sunny and warm.
Great! Are you going to play football?
Yes, I am. And you? What are you going to do?
I'm going to go to the park with my sister.
Nice! Is it going to rain on Sunday?
No, it isn't. It is going to be cloudy.
What are you doing tonight? — I'm having dinner with Sarah.
We're going to launch the new app next month.
Look at the time! We're going to miss our flight!
Don't worry about the report — I'll help you finish it!
I'll call you back in ten minutes, I promise.
I don't think the meeting will take very long.
Take a jacket with you — it might get cold in the evening.
We probably won't have time to visit the museum today.

Tomorrow the weather is going to be great. It is going to be sunny and warm, about twenty-five degrees. We are going to have a picnic in the park. My brother is going to bring the sandwiches and I am going to make a salad. My friends are going to play volleyball. On Sunday it is going to rain, so we are going to stay at home and watch films. Winter is coming, and it is going to be cold soon.

My name is Carlos. I am 30 years old and I am from Brazil. I live in a small apartment in New York. There are two rooms and a kitchen. I work in a restaurant every day from nine to five. I usually have lunch at noon. At the weekend, I like walking in the park and cooking for my friends. Today it is sunny, so I am going to play football with them. I love my new city, but I miss my family.
Hello! I'm Carlos. I live in the apartment next to yours.
Nice to meet you, Carlos. I'm Julia. Where are you from?
I'm from Chicago. Do you work near here?
Yes, I work in a restaurant on Oak Street.
Great! Can you cook Brazilian food?
Yes, I can. Are you free on Saturday? I'm going to cook for my friends.
Welcome back, Marina! How was the conference in Chicago last week?
Thanks, Kevin! It was fantastic, but it was exhausting. There were over five hundred people at the event!
Wow, that's huge! Were the presentations good?
Yes, they were. The keynote speaker on Thursday afternoon was brilliant.
And how was the hotel? Was it near the convention center?
No, it wasn't very close, unfortunately. It was about twenty minutes away by taxi, and there was a lot of traffic every morning.
What about the weather? Was it freezing in Chicago?
Actually, we were really lucky! It wasn't cold at all on Thursday and Friday — it was sunny and around sixty-five degrees.
Nice! By the way, where were you yesterday evening? I called you around seven, and you weren't online.
Oh, I was on the plane back to Boston last night! My flight was delayed for three hours.
Hi Maria! How was your weekend?
It was great. I was at a party on Saturday.
Yes, it was. The music was amazing and the people were very nice.
Some of them were. And you? Where were you?
I was at home. It was a boring weekend, but I was tired.
How was your weekend? — It was really relaxing!
Where were you yesterday afternoon? I called you twice.
Sorry I missed your call — I was in a meeting with a client.
There were a lot of people at the airport last night.
Was the traffic bad this morning? — No, it wasn't bad at all.
Where were you born? — I was born in Curitiba, in 1996.
Our flight was delayed for two hours because of the rain.
He was here at his desk just ten minutes ago!

Last weekend was great. On Saturday we were at my cousin's wedding. The church was beautiful and the music was lovely. We were very happy, but my feet were tired after the party! On Sunday I wasn't at home in the morning because I was at the market. The weather was cold and the streets were empty. In the afternoon my friends were with me and we were all hungry, so we had pizza.

Morning, Lucas! Did you have a good weekend? What did you do?
Morning, Sarah! Yes, I did. On Saturday, I took the train to Niagara Falls with a friend from Brazil.
Oh, nice! How long did the train take?
It took about two hours. We left Toronto at eight in the morning and arrived there around ten.
Did you take the boat tour near the falls?
No, we didn't. We wanted to go on the boat, but the line was huge! So we walked along the river, took a lot of photos, and had lunch at a great restaurant with a view.
What did you do on Sunday? Did you go out too?
No, I didn't go anywhere on Sunday. It rained all afternoon, so I stayed at the hotel, watched a movie, and called my family. What about you?
I met my sister for brunch on Sunday, and we bought a birthday gift for our mom.
What did you do last weekend?
We left at eight in the morning and arrived at ten.
I didn't see your email yesterday — sorry about that!

She bought a new laptop and sent the report last night.

Last summer we visited the mountains. We arrived on Friday and stayed in a small cabin. On Saturday we walked for six hours and we climbed a hill. We didn't take a map, so we asked a farmer for help. In the evening we cooked dinner and played cards. On Sunday it rained, so we didn't go out. We watched the clouds and talked. Did we enjoy it? Yes, we loved it!

Yesterday I took the bus to work. I sat next to a woman, and I found a wallet on the seat. I gave it to the driver. He told me, "Thank you!" The woman saw it and said, "That is my wallet!" She was very happy. She bought me a coffee and we talked for ten minutes. I came to work late, but my boss understood. It was a great day.
Hi Lucy! Did you have a good weekend?
Yes, I did. I went to the beach with my sister.
We took the bus. It was slow, but we saw some beautiful places.
We swam, we ate fish and we sat on the sand all afternoon.

I bought a hat, but I lost it on the bus!

Oh, no! Were you already at the airport when you got the message?
No, I wasn't! While I was taking a taxi to the airport, it started snowing heavily, and the traffic stopped completely.
How stressful! Did you make the flight?
Barely! When I finally arrived at the gate, the other passengers had already boarded, and the crew was closing the door!
Thank goodness you made it! You travel so much now, Lucas. Did you use to travel this much in your old job in Brazil?
No, I didn't use to travel at all! I used to work in the same office every single day. I used to hate flying, but now I love it.
And the snow? Are you used to it yet?
Not really! Back in Brazil I used to drive in heavy rain all the time, but I'm still getting used to driving on ice!

I woke up late, so I missed the bus.

Luckily, a police officer was standing at the corner. He stopped the man and I got my wallet back. After that, I was very careful with my bag.

Yes, I'll come with you. I'll bring some flowers.

In the future, I think people will work fewer hours. Cars will drive themselves and we will talk to computers more. I won't need a map because my phone will tell me everything. But look at the sky: it's going to rain, so I'll take my umbrella. My friend Ana is moving next week. I'll help her carry the boxes, and she'll make lunch. I'm sure it will be a nice day.
